newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK blue chips end off, Beijing Ent steals show.
newsitem.headline: HK blue chips end off, Beijing Ent steals show.

text.p: Hong Kong blue chips took a beating on Thursday, cast out of the limelight by the long-awaited debut of red chip newcomer Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, which tripled in price on its first trading day.
The Hang Seng blue-chip index slid 139.91 points, or 0.96 percent, to 14,416.57 after tumbling to a low of 14,299.01.
"I think it was really a healthy correction today," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
Meanwhile, Beijing Enterprises rocketed to a high of HK$45.00 in early trade before closing the day at HK$40.20. The initial public offering price was HK$12.48.

Brokers said the overall decline in Hong Kong share prices was linked to the expiry on Thursday of May Hang Seng Index futures, which fell 152 points to 14,403. The June contract closed 125 points lower at 14,480.
"There is a certain amount of profit-taking," said Abhijit Chakrabortti, senior strategist at Lehman Brothers. "I suspect the market is not far from fair value."

Without the support of HSBC Holdings, which fell HK$1.00 to HK$228.00, and Hongkong Telecom, which slipped HK$0.30 to HK$16.70, the Hang Seng Index would find it difficult to make any headway, Chakrabortti said.
The biggest losers on Thursday were the property stocks, with Sun Hung Kai Properties down HK$2.25 at HK$92.50, Henderson Land off HK$1.25 at HK$73.00 and Cheung Kong down HK$1.00 at HK$78.00.
"Although the property market has performed well recently, people think the rally will not be as strong as last year," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
"If the property market moves up too fast, they think the government will do something to cool it down and so most property stocks are overvalued," he added.
